title: Patient models distinguish recorded STEMI mortality outcomes
summary: A random-forest model evaluated on an internal holdout from1700 STEMI patients reported ROC areas of0.808 for in-hospital mortality and0.783 for30-day mortality. This source-specific evaluation uses clinical and complication-related inputs; it does not establish a pre-treatment warning tool or improved care.
ai_technology: Random forest; multilayer perceptron; tree ensembles
organization: Govind Ballabh Pant Institute of Post Graduate Medical Education and Research

source_review.scope: Actual relevant primary computational/clinical Methods and high-level Results read; no operational biological protocols inspected

evidence.ai_role: Supervised classifiers learn clinical-feature relationships to observed in-hospital and30-day mortality; SHAP describes model-used features.
evidence.tested: Patients were recruited in2021–2023 and later divided1360/340 for training and internal evaluation, stratified by mortality; resampling was limited to training. The cohort had168 in-hospital and210 thirty-day deaths.
evidence.unknown: Outcome-informed feature screening and data refinement are described before the isolated split, with incomplete nesting detail. Inputs include shock, treatment delay, mechanical complications and echocardiography, so an early pre-treatment prediction time is not established. The paper calls random forest best, but Table3 gives higher30-day ROC areas to other models; no overall-best or significance claim is adopted. Prospective recruitment alone does not establish prospective model validation; no external cohort or treatment benefit was demonstrated.
